name: SpaceX (Space Exploration Technologies Corp.)

summary.text: Space Exploration Technologies Corp., founded in 2002 by Elon Musk and based in Hawthorne, California (listed as Starbase, Texas by one aggregator), designs, manufactures and launches rockets and spacecraft and operates the Starlink satellite internet service. It holds federal contracts with NASA and the Department of Defense and is among the largest U.S. launch providers. Its SEC S-1 was publicly filed on May 20, 2026, and an IPO on Nasdaq under ticker SPCX was reported to be priced on June 11, 2026, under a dual-class structure that gives Musk most of the voting power.

openQuestions: The Reuters pages on SpaceX's board (IPO board stacked with Musk loyalists, May 21, 2026, and board control filing, April 23, 2026) returned HTTP 401, so board composition and Musk's board control are unverified beyond the IR leadership page.
The SEC 8-K of June 16, 2026 was confirmed only as a title and date on the IR site; its contents were not read because the page is a JavaScript app.
The SEC EDGAR page for CIK 1181412 fetched on the roster shows revoked registrations and no filings, which does not match SpaceX; it was not used as a source.

The 2022 Sequoia $800M figure for Musk's Twitter bid and the Botha-SpaceX board link were in the earlier clips but not confirmed on the pages opened: the TechCrunch Twitter article confirms Sequoia's $800M and Musk as Tesla and SpaceX CEO, while Botha's SpaceX board seat is confirmed only by the IR leadership page without a date.

The aVenture page (total raised $9.8B, several 2022-2023 round amounts) and spacexstock.com (which states it is discontinued and has no direct sourcing for many figures) were not used; their totals conflict with FundBat's $11.9B.
Musk's stake (roughly 82% post-IPO) is a single secondary aggregator figure; not confirmed against a primary filing.

No documented evidence was found in this run of federal lobbying outlays, political contribution channels, DOJ/NLRB/FAA enforcement outcomes, Amazon Kuiper FCC disputes, or a documented Anthropic link beyond the Colossus compute contract. Peter Thiel, Mohr Davidow Ventures, PayPal and Amazon connections are not recorded because no source in this run states a relationship with SpaceX.

The fed-spend page reports 52 active federal contracts worth $11.8B and an aggregate $3.3B 2024 revenue figure; these are aggregator figures from USASpending, not verified against USASpending directly.
